messages:
Priya: quick debate — agent vs gateway for OTLP collectors. tradeoffs: local lightweight filtering/sampling at agent, heavy enrichment and archival at gateway. thoughts on per-signal pipelines and exporter routing?
Dan: my instinct: keep agents minimal. do batching, basic sampling, auth. push everything to a central gateway that owns routing/retention. simpler ops and easier to change exporters later. :+1:
Alex: +1 to centralizing routing, but we can't push raw spans that might contain PII upstream un-scrubbed. agents need a small redaction step or field allowlist. otherwise legal/compliance will freak.
Marta: agent redaction ok but be careful about CPU on low-powered hosts. maybe agent does header-based tenant extraction + drop rules, but full attribute processing lives in gateway.
Jake: OTEL collector supports separate pipelines per signal. we can model like:
```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
processors:
  batch:
  tail_sampling:
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [tail_sampling, batch]
      exporters: [tempo, s3-archive]
    metrics:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [k8sattribute, batch]
      exporters: [prometheus_remote_write]
    logs:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [resource_to_telemetry, batch]
      exporters: [log-archive]
```
Jake: with that we can route traces to both tempo (short-term, high-QPS) and S3 for 30d archive. metrics -> remote_write only.
Sam: also consider delivery semantics. traces prefer low-latency small batches; archive exporters can be larger and async. tune send_batch_size and timeout per exporter.
Priya: retention policy: short-term store (tempo) 7d at high QPS, archive 30-90d in object store. need clear cost model for long-tail queries hitting archive.
Dan: gateway should implement disk-backed queue for exporter backpressure. if tempo is down, still accept from agents and drain to S3.
Alex: routing by header X-Org-Id is fine but we need tenant isolation. gateway must apply per-tenant rate limits and sampling policies. otherwise noisy tenants ruin perf.
Marta: agree. where do we keep sampling config? GitOps + dynamic endpoint config pushed to gateway. agents get only a small local policy.
Sam: one more: exporter credentials. we don't want agents to have long-lived creds for external providers. gateway holds secrets and uses short-lived tokens for pushes.
Priya: sounds like we have a pattern: agent = lightweight collector (auth, tenant header, minimal scrub, batching, overflow control), gateway = smart router (enrichment, retention/archival, exporter creds, per-tenant quotas, disk queue).
infra-bot: deploy-notice: collector-gateway v2 is scheduled to canary tomorrow at 10:00 UTC.
Dan: action items:
- Priya: draft reference OTEL config for agent+gateway (include processors and per-exporter batching) — due EOD Thu.
- Alex: list PII patterns and minimal redaction heuristics for agent — due Tue.
- Jake: prototype dual-exporter pattern (tempo + s3) and test backpressure behavior — due next week.
Marta: also add doc for per-tenant sampling + rate-limit enforcement.
Priya: thanks all. i'll post the draft in #eng-platform when ready. :rocket:
